passage: Ojas, your Ajoba will be fine in good hands, but you have that same look I had. I am Harish, your Mama. When I was nine, my Ajoba was in hospital, and the white coats scared me. My father told me the doctors were checking his heart with a machine, and that the beeping was just the machine counting. I asked him, "What if they cannot fix it?" He said, "Then they will tell us honestly, and we will be together." That was enough. I learned the names of two of his medicines and it made the place feel smaller. Ask your mother anything. Understanding helps.

qa.q: What did Harish's father say the beeping was?
qa.a: He said it was the machine counting.

qa.q: Why did learning a little about the doctors' work help nine-year-old Harish?
qa.a: Understanding a little made the hospital feel smaller and cut down his fear, and it helped him trust the doctors.

qa.q: What could Ojas do if the hospital still feels scary?
qa.a: Ojas can ask their parents to explain what the doctors are doing in simple words, and be ready that the outcome may be uncertain.

qa.q: How might Harish's father have felt when the boy asked, "What if they cannot fix it?"
qa.a: He probably felt worried himself but chose to answer honestly and stay close, so his son would not feel alone with the question.

grounding: An elder recalls trusting the doctors by asking simple questions about his grandfather's care; understanding cuts fear while allowing for uncertainty.
